column1:
The FOMC statement remains upbeat—strong labor markets, robust household spending, and inflation near 2 percent with balanced risks and a gradual hiking path. Beige Book evidence adds nuance: districts reported consumer spending increasing, but growth constrained by tight labor availability; wage increases were more common; price pressures varied with notable fuel input costs; and some manufacturers reported constraints tied to labor. These point to capacity and margin pressures even amid solid demand. Layering in the Financial Stability Report’s elevated valuations and higher corporate leverage, plus SLOOS indications of tighter C&I and construction/land development credit and softer loan demand, tilts the outlook modestly more cautious, especially for business fixed investment. Overall stance is still constructive but with greater downside risk from labor constraints and tighter credit.
